answer: An epoch's grading pot is split into three cohorts, lagoon, onyx and meadow, and pays only graders who land on the final median. A bought verdict has a fixed price per identity, yet each extra purchased vote dilutes the payout shared by the cohort, so returns on a purchased majority fall as it grows: the last seats cost most and earn least. Weight never carries between lagoon, onyx and meadow, so one operator must buy a majority three times per round, each time outbidding reviewers whose fallback is an hour of ordinary reading. One honest answer stays cheaper than renting a crowd.
